facts.value: A Western Visayas endemic historically found on Panay, Negros and Guimaras. BirdLife's 2025 account considers the surviving population concentrated in the Central Panay Mountain Range.
Reported mainly in closed-canopy lowland and mid-elevation forest. It feeds in the canopy on figs and other fruits, and nests in large trees.
BirdLife's 2025 IUCN assessment lists Endangered. Older specialist-group accounts list Critically Endangered from 2018. Show the assessment year, not an undated category.

records.caution: Historic Negros or Guimaras records are not current site presence. Avoid disclosing precise nest locations.

records.sourceTitle: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Sulu Hornbill species account

facts.value: A medium-sized, predominantly black hornbill with a white tail. Males have a pale iris; females show a smaller bill and casque and a darker eye.
Associated with primary lowland and mountain rainforest. Large cavity-bearing trees are necessary for nesting; fruit is a major food item.
Endemic to the Sulu archipelago; recent verified persistence is concentrated on Tawi-Tawi rather than all historic islands.

records.caution: Retain uncertainty around older island records and population estimates; photograph safely without disturbing active nest trees.

records.sourceTitle: BirdLife International, Threatened Birds of Asia, Sulu Bleeding-heart historical species account

facts.value: A Philippine Sulu-archipelago endemic known with certainty from historical Tawi-Tawi specimens in the cited account.
Reported records from other Sulu islands were not confirmed in the historical review. Museum evidence should not be treated as proof of modern wild occurrence.

records.caution: Modern abundance, field characters, activity and habitat suitability remain insufficiently documented for a reliable phone identification key.

records.sourceTitle: IUCN Red List, Negros Bleeding-heart assessment, 2018

facts.value: A short-tailed ground dove with an iridescent green head and mantle, a narrow red breast patch on a pale chest, and contrasting pale wing markings.
The account describes dense forest understorey and forest-floor foraging, including some secondary and logged forest on Panay.
Endemic to Panay and Negros. Historical island records do not establish a current occupied site.

records.caution: The cited global conservation assessment is dated 2018. Similar bleeding-heart species and age variation require field photographs and comparison.

records.sourceTitle: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Visayan Hornbill

facts.value: A relatively small hornbill with markedly different male and female plumage. Males show pale yellowish-white areas with dark upperparts; females are much darker.
Reported in lowland primary and secondary rainforests, visiting fruiting trees. Fruit forms the majority of its documented diet.
The specialist description notes a rapid, noisy series of calls; store original audio rather than guessing a species from an unreviewed recording.

records.caution: Keep male, female and juvenile plumage distinct. A tarictic-hornbill label alone is not a diagnostic identification.

records.sourceTitle: iNaturalist taxon summary, Visayan Broadbill, drawing on published taxonomy

facts.value: The source lists Samar, Leyte and Bohol as endemic island range, not nationwide occurrence.
Summarized as a bird of tropical moist lowland forest; no specific site or current elevation is inferred.
Formerly treated within a wider broadbill concept and now recognized separately from the wattled broadbill.

records.caution: An iNaturalist taxon summary is a secondary overview. Detailed plumage keys and current national threat category still need original literature.

records.sourceTitle: Oiseaux.net, Whiskered Pitta ecology and regional account

facts.value: A Luzon endemic associated with mountain forest, commonly at elevations near or above 1,000 m in published accounts.
A mainly terrestrial, day-active invertebrate-foraging pitta; the cited reference describes feeding in forest ground vegetation.
Aural detections should retain sound recordings and conditions. A ground bird glimpsed briefly is not sufficient for species-level ID.

records.caution: Distinguish this taxon from other Philippine pittas using specialist characters, not the presence of montane forest alone.

records.sourceTitle: IUCN Red List, Black-belted/Visayan Flowerpecker, 2022 assessment

facts.value: A small, canopy-feeding flowerpecker. The described male has glossy dark upperparts, pale underparts, a black breast bar and a red central belly streak.
Endemic to Western Visayas, with records chiefly from Panay and Negros; former Guimaras occurrence remains uncertain.
Primary, secondary and degraded forest near taller forest are included in the assessment's lowland and hill habitat summary.

records.caution: Separate this species from Dicaeum australe using the breast bar and the appropriate sex/age; do not extrapolate a current IUCN category from an old source snapshot.

records.sourceTitle: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Barbourula busuangensis

facts.value: Known from Palawan, Busuanga, Culion and Balabac according to the museum taxonomy account; no Philippine-wide range should be assumed.
The original type locality was a small stream on Busuanga. The museum account references a later study of vocalizations.
A member of Bombinatoridae, not an ordinary rainforest tree frog.

records.caution: Water habitat is historical locality evidence, not a validated species-wide microhabitat model or local detection.

records.sourceTitle: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Platymantis spelaeus

facts.value: The source describes limestone karst areas of southern Negros, with published records in roughly 20–400 m elevations.
The type locality is a limestone cave in southern Negros Oriental.
The form Platymantis spelaea is recorded as an incorrect later spelling; retain the checklist's accepted name.

records.caution: Karst habitat does not identify a frog by itself. A species-level diagnosis needs call and comparative morphological evidence.

records.sourceTitle: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Platymantis paengi

facts.value: Originally described from northwestern Panay, with a subsequently published Sibuyan Island report requiring geographic and taxonomic context.
The original 2007 description documents morphology, advertisement calls and natural history; a 2022 source discusses population differences.
The common name Panay Limestone Frog names the type-associated population; it is not a general identification for any karst frog.

records.caution: Published Sibuyan records and vocal differences require specialist comparison; do not generalize a single call or locality.

records.sourceTitle: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Platymantis hazelae

facts.value: Reported from mountainous Negros and Masbate forests, including elevations in the 600–1,700 m band in the cited summary.
The AMNH account notes an older Philautus combination and provisional earlier synonym questions.

records.caution: Mountain elevation or a 'forest frog' appearance does not demonstrate identification; retain photographs, calls and taxon uncertainty.

records.sourceTitle: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Platymantis rabori

facts.value: Published rainforest records on Bohol, Leyte, Samar and Mindanao, approximately 300–1,400 m in the museum account.
The taxon was confused with Platymantis guentheri prior to its description; the original literature placed it in that comparison group.

records.caution: Older records under other Platymantis names need expert name reconciliation; do not assign rabori from region or elevation alone.

records.sourceTitle: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Leptobrachium lumadorum

facts.value: The source describes south and central Mindanao, with later regional material from Basilan and Samar.
Earlier authors confused these Philippine litter frogs with Leptobrachium hasseltii before formal description.
The museum account cites recent field habitat work in the Mount Gutom and Agusan regions.

records.caution: Taxonomic complexes can contain difficult lookalikes. Verify the study's locality and identification method before interpreting any new record.

records.sourceTitle: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Leptobrachium mangyanorum

facts.value: Documented from Mindoro with a possible neighboring Semirara report flagged by the museum source.
Originally described from a river locality on Mindoro, and formerly grouped with Leptobrachium hasseltii.
The source places this taxon within a Leptobrachium montanum species complex needing comparative identification.

records.caution: Possible Semirara distribution is not confirmed station occurrence. Avoid extending it to other islands without an explicit paper.

records.sourceTitle: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Limnonectes magnus

facts.value: The taxonomic account includes published records across the Mindanao faunal region, with later reports requiring post-2021 systematic review.
Recent research reinterpreted the original Mount Apo type locality and the application of the name to lowland Mindanao populations.
Philippine field publications cited in the account document stream and river-associated encounters across eastern and western Mindanao.

records.caution: Older records grouped under Rana macrodon or historic Limnonectes species concepts cannot be equated automatically with this name.

records.sourceTitle: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Ansonia mcgregori

facts.value: The museum account places this endemic toad in the mountains of central and western Mindanao.
Once synonymized with Ansonia muelleri and later reinstated; molecular work found possible unnamed western Mindanao lineages.
Published geographic-call research notes variation that may include undescribed diversity.

records.caution: Do not assign the species from skin pattern or a single call without geographic and specialist cross-checks.

records.sourceTitle: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Pelophryne lighti

facts.value: Reported in Philippine lowland and montane riverine forests, including Mindanao, Samar, Leyte and Bohol.
Originally described as Nectophryne lighti from the Mindanao region in 1920.
The museum source cites regional accounts in Samar and Agusan Marsh from 2026.

records.caution: Published locality references require their collection methods and date; calling activity and exact microhabitat remain unassessed for this card.

records.sourceTitle: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Sanguirana everetti

facts.value: Described from the Zamboanga region on Mindanao, with a long taxonomic history under Rana and other combinations.
The current museum summary recognizes a more limited southwestern Mindanao faunal scope, with some neighboring-island records uncertain.
The source explicitly notes transfer of historical Visayan populations to Sanguirana acai.

records.caution: Avoid converting earlier records for the Sanguirana everetti complex into verified present-day everetti determinations.
